newsitem.title: USA: U.S. utilities seek credits under climate plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. utilities seek credits under climate plan.

text.p: U.S. utilities on Thursday urged President Clinton to ensure that any global climate treaty included credits for companies that made pollution cuts ahead of treaty deadlines, involved developing countries, and provided flexibility for meeting emissions cuts.

"Each of these concepts .. is a vital and necessary component of any effort to address greenhouse gas emissions and, therefore, must be included in any agreement adopted in Kyoto," the Edison Electric Institute, which represents investor-owned utilities, said in a July 24 letter to Clinton.

The letter was sent on the day when Clinton hosted a meeting with seven leading scientists to draw attention to the need for setting limits on carbon emissions from the burning of fossil fuels in order to slow global warming.

The White House is trying to convince the public to support a climate treaty due to be signed at the end of this year in Kyoto that will set binding targets for carbon emissions cuts in industrialized countries.

Edison Electric Institute said it could not support a treaty with binding targets because scientists had not yet quantified how much of an impact human activities have on climate change and the economic costs would be huge.

"We believe that greenhouse gas emissions should be addressed through commitments by industries to flexible, cost-effective, comprehensive (ie. all greenhouse gases, sources and sinks) and voluntary actions," EEI president Tom Kuhn said in the letter.

He reiterated the industry's view that if companies in industrialized countries had to cut their emissions while their competitors in developing countries did not, rich nations would be at a competitive disadvantage.
